title: Securing the quantum stack: export controls, choke points and strategic competition
gist: Since 2024 the US and allies have built broadly aligned but legally distinct national export controls across the whole quantum computing stack — materials, equipment and components — bypassing a Wassenaar Arrangement deadlocked by Russia since 2022. The controls bind hardest where production is concentrated in allied jurisdictions (dilution refrigerators from Bluefors and Oxford Instruments, synthetic diamond from Element Six), leak at the materials layer (helium-3, quantum-grade diamond, silicon-28 partly sited in Russia and China), and are already provoking Chinese indigenisation; the authors argue leverage decays unless allied governments also sustain demand for the very firms their control lists designate as critical.

themes.theme: Wassenaar deadlock and the plurilateral workaround

insights.claim: Russia's obstruction of Wassenaar Arrangement control-list updates since 2022 has pushed the US and like-minded states to coordinate quantum export controls through plurilateral arrangements outside the formal multilateral regime.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Technology-denial policy is migrating to ad hoc coalitions, so compliance risk for exporters now depends on tracking a dozen national lists rather than one treaty list.
insights.quote: The result is a patchwork of broadly harmonised, but legally distinct, export-control regimes.
insights.locator: Since 2024, the United States and several allies

insights.claim: The US Bureau of Industry and Security's September 2024 Interim Final Rule set quantum-computer control thresholds by qubit count and error rate, and added worldwide licensing requirements plus outbound-investment restrictions aimed at China's quantum sector.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Performance-threshold controls mean the binding constraint moves as machines improve — watch qubit/error-rate milestones as regulatory trigger points, not just as technical news.
insights.quote: with control thresholds defined by qubit counts and error rates – in effect, how large and how reliable a machine is
insights.locator: National measures

insights.claim: Washington deliberately softened its own quantum rule by granting licence exceptions to countries with equivalent controls — Australia, Japan, the Netherlands, Norway and the UK — and by replacing deemed-export restrictions on foreign nationals with mere record-keeping.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: A rare loosening signals policymakers fear talent and research friction more than diversion risk — a template that could be copied in AI and biotech controls.
insights.quote: This represents a marked departure from conventional American export-control practice
insights.locator: Recognising that quantum innovation depends on international collaboration

insights.claim: Executive Order 14413, 'Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation', issued in June 2026, ties US quantum denial policy to harmonisation with allies, alongside a 13-country Quantum Development Group forum.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Formal allied coordination machinery is the leading indicator of where the next control-list expansions land.
insights.locator: Under US President Donald Trump’s second administration

insights.claim: Because EU Dual-use Regulation 2021/821 is tied to multilateral regimes, six member states — Finland, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Spain — had to use Article 9 national controls, fragmenting the single market until the Commission introduced autonomous EU-level quantum controls in September 2025.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Intra-EU regulatory fragmentation created arbitrage windows for buyers; the new '500-series' closes them and raises compliance burden on European quantum suppliers.
insights.quote: Although this preserved alignment with Washington, it also created regulatory fragmentation within the single market.
insights.locator: Within the European Union, institutional constraints

insights.claim: The EU's new '500-series' of EU-only dual-use entries covering quantum computing has been in force since November 2025, and in December 2025 the UK mirrored it by replacing its national PL9013–9015 entries with 500-series controls.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Convergence on a single list format across the EU and UK reduces the leakage seam that Chinese buyers exploited in 2022.
insights.locator: Other allies followed a similar path

themes.theme: Choke points inside the three-layer quantum stack

insights.claim: The efficacy of quantum export controls depends less on how comprehensive the control lists are than on whether they capture the handful of dispersed firms and facilities whose technologies are indispensable, hard to substitute and sited in cooperating jurisdictions.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Screen the quantum supply chain for irreplaceable, allied-domiciled nodes — those firms carry policy-driven pricing power and acquisition-target value.
insights.quote: The effectiveness of any export-control regime will therefore depend less on the comprehensiveness of its control lists than on whether it captures the small number of geographically dispersed firms and facilities
insights.locator: The quantum stack and its choke points

insights.claim: At the materials layer the binding scarcities are isotopically enriched silicon-28 for spin qubits, available commercially from only a few facilities worldwide, and helium-3 for dilution refrigeration, a scarce by-product of tritium decay concentrated in US and Russian stockpiles.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Helium-3 and enriched isotope capacity are single-point failure risks for any superconducting or spin-qubit roadmap — supply shocks there hit every hardware developer at once.
insights.locator: Where these nodes sit becomes visible only when the supply chain is disaggregated

insights.claim: Electronic-grade synthetic diamond, the substrate for many quantum-sensing and quantum-memory devices, is dominated in the West by Element Six, the UK-based De Beers subsidiary described as the only proven Western supplier of quantum-grade material.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: A single De Beers subsidiary is a Western monopoly node in quantum sensing — rare strategic optionality inside a mining group not valued as a quantum play.
insights.quote: the ‘only proven Western supplier’ of quantum-grade material
insights.locator: electronic-grade synthetic diamond

insights.claim: Superconducting quantum computers cannot operate without dilution refrigerators, produced at scale by only a handful of suppliers led by Bluefors in Finland and Oxford Instruments in the UK.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Cryogenics vendors are the physical gatekeepers of the superconducting architecture — their order books are a cleaner read on quantum capex than qubit-count press releases.
insights.locator: At the equipment layer

insights.claim: Europe hosts fewer frontier quantum-computing firms than the US but holds disproportionate leverage across the enabling layers of the stack, making Brussels' regulatory choices decisive for any allied denial strategy.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Europe's quantum relevance is in picks-and-shovels, not qubit champions — the investable exposure is in equipment and components, not headline platforms.
insights.quote: Europe fields fewer frontier quantum-computing firms than the US, yet it holds disproportionate leverage across the enabling layers
insights.locator: At the component layer

themes.theme: Anticipatory containment as a new control doctrine

insights.claim: Unlike controls on mature technologies, which start downstream in the supply chain and tighten upstream over time, quantum controls were applied across nearly the whole stack from the outset to shape the ecosystem before it matures.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Expect the same front-loaded, whole-stack template on the next emerging technology — firms in nascent fields should assume controls arrive pre-commercialisation.
insights.quote: In effect, on quantum, governments are moving from reactive regulation to anticipatory containment, seeking to constrain future military capabilities before they become commercially widespread.
insights.locator: Quantum computing illustrates how export controls on emerging technologies

insights.claim: The core design tension in quantum export controls is preventing military exploitation by rivals without throttling the scientific research, commercialisation and innovation on which the controlling side's own lead depends.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Policy will keep oscillating between tightening and carve-outs; licence exceptions and research safeguards are the pressure valve to monitor.
insights.quote: The central challenge is balancing two competing objectives
insights.locator: Quantum computing illustrates how export controls on emerging technologies

insights.claim: No single country dominates the quantum supply chain across materials, cryogenic equipment, hardware, software, fabrication and algorithms, which makes the ecosystem inherently international and unusually hard to fence.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Denial strategies here need many jurisdictions to hold the line simultaneously — a single defecting supplier state undoes the regime.
insights.locator: The quantum stack and its choke points

insights.claim: After the UK refused an export licence for Oxford Instruments equipment in 2022, the Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences simply bought three dilution refrigerators from Finland's Bluefors, before Finland had finalised its own control list.
insights.speaker: IISS
entities: Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences
insights.so_what: A concrete demonstration that a choke point with two suppliers in two jurisdictions is no choke point until both align — timing gaps are the exploitable seam.
insights.quote: the Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences purchased three dilution refrigerators from Bluefors – at a time when Finland’s own control list had yet to be finalised
insights.locator: Where the controls bind – and where they leak

insights.claim: Helium-3 and quantum-grade diamond fall largely outside the quantum-specific control lists and are governed instead by older, unevenly applied provisions, leaving the materials layer only partially covered.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: The least-controlled layer is the one with the fewest substitutes — a plausible target for the next round of listings.
insights.locator: At the materials layer, by contrast, coverage is partial

insights.claim: Part of the world's limited silicon-28 enrichment capability sits in Russia and China, so listing the material creates a dependency for Western programmes rather than leverage over rivals.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Control lists can flag Western vulnerabilities as much as adversary ones — read new listings as a map of where the West is exposed to counter-restriction.
insights.quote: making a listed material as much a dependency as a lever
insights.locator: Moreover, listing an item in itself does not confer leverage

insights.claim: Export restrictions function as a signalling device that advertises which dependencies a rival should eliminate, and China has responded by indigenising the listed items.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Each listing carries an induced-substitution cost; the half-life of a choke point shortens as soon as it is published.
insights.quote: Export restrictions do not merely deny; they signal. Each controlled item advertises a dependency worth eliminating, and China has responded accordingly.
insights.locator: The controls falter where the underlying node is contestable

insights.claim: Within two years of the first Western listings, Chinese entities QuantumCTek and the Anhui Quantum Computing Engineering Research Centre had begun factory production of a domestic dilution refrigerator, while diamond-substrate supplier Chenguang Machinery & Electric Equipment moved to court academics deterred by Western restrictions.
insights.speaker: IISS
entities: Anhui Quantum Computing Engineering Research Centre
insights.so_what: Two years is the observed substitution lag for a hardware choke point — a benchmark for how long any quantum denial advantage lasts.
insights.locator: Within two years of the first Western listings

insights.claim: Where the production base is broad — control electronics, lasers, much of photonics — export controls only raise costs and buy time because supply chains reconfigure through alternative jurisdictions faster than lists can be updated.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Distinguish friction nodes from denial nodes when pricing policy risk: only the concentrated nodes carry durable strategic rents.
insights.quote: Controls on such nodes function as friction, not denial: they slow acquisition without preventing it.
insights.locator: Where the production base is broader

insights.claim: Quantum-technology dependence is mutual: Beijing restricts exports of sub-6-kelvin cryogenic technology and quantum encryption even while Chinese programmes rely on US and Russian helium-3 stockpiles.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Escalation in quantum controls is two-sided; Chinese cryogenic and encryption restrictions are an underpriced retaliation channel.
insights.quote: Dependence, moreover, runs both ways: Beijing restricts exports of sub-6-kelvin cryogenic technology and quantum encryption, even as China’s own programmes rely on US and Russian helium-3 stockpiles.
insights.locator: Dependence, moreover, runs both ways

themes.theme: Denial must be matched by absorption

insights.claim: Export controls cannot secure quantum leadership alone because they must be paired with resilient critical-mineral supply chains, investment screening against foreign acquisition of strategic firms, and industrial policy that lets promising companies commercialise and scale.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Treat controls, screening and subsidy as one integrated toolkit — policy announcements in any one leg change the outlook for the others.
insights.quote: Together, export controls, investment screening and industrial policy form an integrated toolkit for shaping the early quantum market.
insights.locator: From anticipation to absorption

insights.claim: In May 2026 the US administration signed letters of intent to invest US$2 billion for minority equity stakes in nine quantum companies, with two-thirds directed to two dedicated quantum-chip foundries — IBM's new Anderon facility and GlobalFoundries — to build domestic quantum-grade wafer manufacturing.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: The state is taking direct equity in quantum hardware; wafer-foundry capacity, not qubit counts, is where the public money is concentrating.
insights.quote: Two-thirds of this investment was directed to two dedicated quantum-chip foundries
insights.locator: In 2018 the US enacted the National Quantum Initiative Act

insights.claim: Allied quantum industrial policy is now sizeable and explicit: the UK has committed £2.5bn to a 2024–34 National Quantum Strategy with a dedicated public-procurement programme, the EU invests through a €1bn Quantum Technologies Flagship, and Japan designated 2025 its 'first year of quantum industrialisation'.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Public procurement and flagship budgets are the near-term revenue source for quantum vendors long before commercial demand arrives.
insights.locator: The UK committed £2.5bn

insights.claim: Choke-point leverage decays if the designated firms lose customers: a dilution-refrigerator maker or isotope-enrichment facility is only a strategic asset while it remains a viable company, so controls that shrink its market or scare buyers away destroy the leverage they were meant to create.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: Licensing uncertainty is a demand risk for the very equipment vendors governments depend on — watch for offsetting state procurement or equity support at those firms.
insights.quote: Choke-point leverage is an asset with maintenance costs: a dilution-refrigerator maker or an isotope-enrichment facility remains a strategic asset only for as long as it remains a viable company.
insights.locator: But the toolkit’s logic points beyond anticipatory containment

insights.claim: As quantum moves from laboratory to deployment, the strategic question shifts from which technologies to deny an adversary to which nodes of one's own ecosystem to sustain.
insights.speaker: IISS
insights.so_what: The next policy wave should be demand-side support for allied choke-point firms rather than more listings — a tailwind for European and Japanese enabling-layer suppliers.
insights.quote: the decisive question is no longer which technologies to deny an adversary, but which nodes of one’s own ecosystem to sustain
insights.locator: Denial therefore has to be matched by absorption
